definition: Compunction means a pang of guilt about doing something wrong.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word compunction. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know compunction should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: He returned the overdue books with real compunction, having loudly blamed the library's records all semester.
A twinge of conscience is far slighter than compunction — the faintest flicker, noticed, then gone by lunch, while compunction keeps pricking until the wrong is put right.
Remorse goes further than compunction — compunction pricks over a wrong still small enough to fix; remorse aches for years over harm already done.

A qualm is a flicker of conscience that arrives before the act — the uneasy pause with your hand already on the door. Compunction usually arrives during or after: the pang of guilt over a wrong already done, sharp enough to push you back to repair it.

A scruple is the standing principle that balks — the fixed rule inside you that refuses certain acts, whether or not you feel anything. Compunction is the felt sting itself: the actual pang pricking you over one particular wrong. Scruples stop the act beforehand; compunction needles you afterward.

Maya's poster won the school science fair, and for one whole afternoon she let herself enjoy the ribbon and the applause.
But the winning idea — testing pond water at three different depths — had come from her lab partner, Ruth, and Maya had let the judges believe it was hers alone.
That night the compunction set in: a sharp, insistent pang of guilt that returned every time her eyes landed on the ribbon.
It was not vague, all-purpose regret.
It pointed at one specific wrong, and it kept pricking at her until she did something about it.
The next morning she found the fair director, had the entry corrected to include Ruth's name, and only then did the pang finally loosen and let her go.
